title: A Day in Ancient Rome (sample)
claimsToVerify: Many Romans lived in crowded apartment blocks; kitchens were rare in them
Wealthy patrons received clients at dawn
Public baths were social as well as hygienic spaces

scenes.text: Imagine waking up in Rome two thousand years ago. No alarm, no electricity, no running water. Just the sounds of a city already coming awake.
scenes.imagePrompt: Ancient Roman rooftops at dawn, oil lamps glowing in windows

scenes.text: Most people lived in crowded apartment blocks. Rooms were small, often shared, and kitchens were rare, so cooking at home was a luxury for many.
scenes.imagePrompt: Narrow multi-storey Roman apartment building at night with a single lit window

scenes.text: Breakfast, if you had it, was simple. Bread, maybe some cheese or olives, grabbed quickly before heading out into the street.
Wealthy Romans received visitors at dawn. Clients in togas waited to greet their patron, hoping for a favor, a meal, or a little money.
scenes.imagePrompt: Crowd of men in togas waiting at the entrance hall of a wealthy Roman villa

scenes.text: Meanwhile, shopkeepers opened their stalls, craftsmen started work, and the street filled with noise.
By early afternoon, many people headed to the public baths. They were part gym, part spa, and part social club.
scenes.imagePrompt: Roman public baths with steam and bathers relaxing, warm light

scenes.text: You moved between warm and hot rooms, exercised, chatted, and caught up on the news of the day.
That is one ordinary day in the Roman world. Different from ours in many ways, yet strangely familiar. Next time, we step into an Egyptian village.
scenes.imagePrompt: Roman street at dusk with lamps being lit
